extracted.intended_audience: journalists, editors, journalism students, and news organizations
extracted.subtask_description: A professional code setting ethical standards and practical guidance for journalists across media on gathering, reporting, and publishing news. It outlines principles (seek truth, minimize harm, act independently, be accountable) and specific behavioral expectations for reporters and news organizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to seek truth and provide a fair, comprehensive account
rubrics_metrics.description: The duty of the journalist is to further public enlightenment by seeking truth and providing a fair and comprehensive account of events and issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conscientious journalists from all media and specialties strive to serve the public with thoroughness and honesty; professional integrity is the cornerstone of credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Code is a voluntary resource, not legally enforceable
rubrics_metrics.description: The SPJ Code of Ethics is voluntarily embraced by thousands of journalists and is intended as a resource for ethical decision‑making, not a set of legally enforceable rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Code cannot be legally enforced under the First Amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be honest, fair and courageous in gathering, reporting and interpreting information
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists should be honest, fair and courageous in gathering, reporting and interpreting information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Test accuracy and avoid inadvertent error; never deliberately distort
rubrics_metrics.description: Test the accuracy of information from all sources and exercise care to avoid inadvertent error. Deliberate distortion is never permissible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diligently seek response from subjects accused of wrongdoing
rubrics_metrics.description: Diligently seek out subjects of news stories to give them the opportunity to respond to allegations of wrongdoing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify sources whenever feasible
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify sources whenever feasible; the public is entitled to as much information as possible on sources' reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Question motives before promising anonymity; clarify and keep promises
rubrics_metrics.description: Always question sources' motives before promising anonymity. Clarify conditions attached to any promise made in exchange for information. Keep promises.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid misrepresentation in headlines, promos and other formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Make certain that headlines, news teases and promotional material, photos, video, audio, graphics, sound bites and quotations do not misrepresent; they should not oversimplify or highlight incidents out of context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Never distort news photos or video; label montages and illustrations
rubrics_metrics.description: Never distort the content of news photos or video. Image enhancement for technical clarity is always permissible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid misleading re-enactments; label necessary re-enactments
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid misleading re-enactments or staged news events. If re-enactment is necessary to tell a story, label it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use undercover or surreptitious methods only when necessary and explain them
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid undercover or other surreptitious methods of gathering information except when traditional open methods will not yield information vital to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of such methods should be explained as part of the story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Never plagiarize
rubrics_metrics.description: Never plagiarize.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tell diverse and broad human stories boldly
rubrics_metrics.description: Tell the story of the diversity and magnitude of the human experience boldly, even when it is unpopular to do so.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examine and avoid imposing one's own cultural values
rubrics_metrics.description: Examine their own cultural values and avoid imposing those values on others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid stereotyping across listed categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid stereotyping by race, gender, age, religion, ethnicity, geography, sexual orientation, disability, physical appearance or social status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support open exchange of views, including repugnant ones
rubrics_metrics.description: Support the open exchange of views, even views they find repugnant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Give voice to the voiceless; consider official and unofficial sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Give voice to the voiceless; official and unofficial sources of information can be equally valid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish advocacy from news reporting; label analysis and commentary
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguish between advocacy and news reporting. Analysis and commentary should be labeled and not misrepresent fact or context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish news from advertising; avoid hybrids that blur lines
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguish news from advertising and shun hybrids that blur the lines between the two.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure public business is conducted openly; promote access to government records
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize a special obligation to ensure that the public's business is conducted in the open and that government records are open to inspection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show compassion to sources, subjects and colleagues
rubrics_metrics.description: Ethical journalists treat sources, subjects and colleagues as human beings deserving of respect; show compassion for those who may be affected adversely by news coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use special sensitivity when dealing with children and inexperienced sources or subjects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be sensitive when interviewing or photographing those affected by tragedy or grief
rubrics_metrics.description: Be sensitive when seeking or using interviews or photographs of those affected by tragedy or grief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize reporting may cause harm; pursuit is not license for arrogance
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that gathering and reporting information may cause harm or discomfort. Pursuit of the news is not a license for arrogance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect greater privacy rights of private individuals; intrude only for overriding public need
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that private people have a greater right to control information about themselves than do public officials and others who seek power, influence or attention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only an overriding public need can justify intrusion into anyone's privacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show good taste; avoid pandering to lurid curiosity
rubrics_metrics.description: Show good taste. Avoid pandering to lurid curiosity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be cautious identifying juvenile suspects or victims of sex crimes
rubrics_metrics.description: Be cautious about identifying juvenile suspects or victims of sex crimes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be judicious about naming criminal suspects before formal charges
rubrics_metrics.description: Be judicious about naming criminal suspects before the formal filing of charges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance suspects' fair trial rights with the public's right to be informed
rubrics_metrics.description: Balance a criminal suspect's fair trial rights with the public's right to be informed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid conflicts of interest, real or perceived
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists should avoid conflicts of interest, real or perceived.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remain free of associations that compromise integrity or credibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Remain free of associations and activities that may compromise integrity or damage credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refuse gifts, favors and special treatment that compromise integrity
rubrics_metrics.description: Refuse gifts, favors, fees, free travel and special treatment, and shun secondary employment, political involvement, public office and service in community organizations if they compromise journalistic integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclose unavoidable conflicts
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclose unavoidable conflicts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be vigilant and courageous in holding the powerful accountable
rubrics_metrics.description: Be vigilant and courageous about holding those with power accountable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deny favored treatment to advertisers and special interests
rubrics_metrics.description: Deny favored treatment to advertisers and special interests and resist their pressure to influence news coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be wary of paid or incentivized sources; avoid bidding for news
rubrics_metrics.description: Be wary of sources offering information for favors or money; avoid bidding for news.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarify and explain coverage; invite public dialogue over conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarify and explain news coverage and invite dialogue with the public over journalistic conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage the public to voice grievances against the media
rubrics_metrics.description: Encourage the public to voice grievances against the news media.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admit mistakes and correct them promptly
rubrics_metrics.description: Admit mistakes and correct them promptly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expose unethical practices of journalists and media organizations
rubrics_metrics.description: Expose unethical practices of journalists and the news media.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abide by the same high standards applied to others
rubrics_metrics.description: Abide by the same high standards to which they hold others.
